statements.status_notes: A TLS server whose sni_callback switches SSLSocket.context to another SSLContext could crash or call through a freed pointer when nothing else kept the original context alive, triggerable by a remote unauthenticated client. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/156293 (3.10 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/ec44b5a3258cbda947d5e07242ee562ed05ef24b), first released in CPython 3.10.22, the security release that carries it for the 3.10 branch; see the advisory https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/QMQIUQB6WGGC3MI7I3WKQXOYOBDSPPS3/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19445. The DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.10 package is fixed from 3.10.22-r0, the first published build of CPython 3.10.22 (the version string in libpython3.10.so); no earlier published build carries a backport. Checked the compiled _ssl extension module in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.22-r8) against the upstream Modules/_ssl.c: upstream 3.10.22 drops the SSL_CTX_set_tlsext_servername_arg registration and adds a servername-callback reset in context deallocation. The calls to SSL_CTX_ctrl with SSL_CTRL_SET_TLSEXT_SERVERNAME_ARG and to SSL_CTX_callback_ctrl with SSL_CTRL_SET_TLSEXT_SERVERNAME_CB are one and three in 3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.21-r2 (as in upstream 3.10.21 and earlier) and none and four from 3.10.22-r0 on (as in upstream 3.10.22).

A TLS server whose sni_callback switches SSLSocket.context to another SSLContext could crash or call through a freed pointer when nothing else kept the original context alive, triggerable by a remote unauthenticated client. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/156293 (3.15 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/63fab143d94cafae71850831acfb52041ba44af7) before the 3.15.0 final release: the fix first shipped in CPython 3.15.0rc3, and the CVE record lists 3.15 as affected only before 3.15.0rc3; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/QMQIUQB6WGGC3MI7I3WKQXOYOBDSPPS3/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19445. The fix stops registering the context as the servername callback argument (SSL_CTX_set_tlsext_servername_arg, which calls SSL_CTX_ctrl with SSL_CTRL_SET_TLSEXT_SERVERNAME_ARG) and adds a servername-callback reset when a context is freed, so Modules/_ssl.c goes from one servername-arg call and two servername-callback calls in 3.15.0rc2 to none and three in 3.15.0rc3, 3.15.0 and 3.15.2. Disassembled the compiled _ssl extension module in the python-3.15 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository by 2026-11-27 (3.15.0-r0 and 3.15.2-r0 to 3.15.2-r4), on x86_64 and aarch64 (each build is CPython 3.15.0 or 3.15.2 by the version string in its libpython3.15.so): every build calls SSL_CTX_ctrl with SSL_CTRL_SET_TLSEXT_SERVERNAME_ARG zero times and SSL_CTX_callback_ctrl with SSL_CTRL_SET_TLSEXT_SERVERNAME_CB three times, matching the fixed source; the same count finds the servername-arg call once in the _ssl module of an earlier unfixed DHI Python build (python-3.14 3.14.3-r0). Every published build carries the fix, so the range ends at the lowest published build, 3.15.0-r0.
